notes_for_human: VERIFICATION RESULT re: 'clearance eligibility' claim — CONFIRMED for exactly one role type, NOT a blanket policy. The general 'Software Engineer, Internship' posting (Palo Alto) lists 'Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance' — but under a 'What We Value' heading (a preference signal), not 'What We Require.' Counterintuitively, the two Forward Deployed Software Engineer internship postings checked — including the one explicitly titled 'US Government' — contain zero mention of clearance, citizenship, or sponsorship anywhere in their full raw HTML (confirmed by direct grep, not just a skim). So the tracker's flat 'requires clearance eligibility' is accurate for the general SWE Intern req and NOT demonstrated for the FDSE Commercial or FDSE US Government reqs sampled here. Caveat: other FDSE reqs exist (Intel, AUS Government, Defense Tech, Year at Palantir variants — see URLs below) that were not individually fetched due to the 4-8 call budget; a role literally titled 'US Government' lacking clearance language is unusual enough that I'd want a second FDSE Government req cross-checked before treating the pattern as firm. No posting found under the exact names 'Winternship' or 'Path' on the live lever.co board as of this check — those may be informal/legacy names not currently in use, or simply not open right now; could not confirm either way. No 'Summer 20XX' cycle string or explicit open/close dates appear on any of the three postings checked — all cycle/opens/closes fields are genuinely unstated on-page, not omissions on my part. Unfetched FDSE/other req URLs surfaced by search, for follow-up if needed: https://jobs.lever.co/palantir/9e40d77f-b07c-437b-98e7-def9b0184d89 (Intel), https://jobs.lever.co/palantir/395a4483-fc3d-4b77-a500-501923fd0976 (AUS Government), https://jobs.lever.co/palantir/f17e98d0-046a-4e6e-9d65-ed0b12dd0ff7 (Defense Tech), https://jobs.lever.co/palantir/e6ff8bf2-135e-474d-ad37-24f490ae1dd2 (another 'US Government' req id, different from the one checked). Technical note: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on all three jobs.lever.co URLs; plain curl with a browser User-Agent string succeeded (200) on all three — lever.co appears to be blocking WebFetch's default UA/fingerprint specifically, not blocking scraping generally.
